task: What's the most likely cause of this webhook failure, and in what order should I check things?
text:
Our support desk stopped creating tickets from the CRM webhook last night. Every delivery gets 'HTTP 401: signature mismatch' in the integration log. Config excerpt:

helpdesk:
  base_url: https://support.internal.example
  api_token: tok-demo-9Vq2Lm7XcR4t
  webhook_secret: hooksig-31d8b0e7a2-fake
  retry: 3
  timeout_s: 20

Nothing changed in the YAML, but Mattias rotated the webhook secret on the CRM side at about 23:10. Tickets created through the web form still arrive fine. The only customer affected so far is Halvorsen Freight, our largest enterprise account; their contract has a service credit of 18,500 euros per breached day if P1 tickets aren't logged within 30 minutes, so this is urgent.

decisions.label: SECRET
decisions.reason: A live helpdesk API token must never leave the company; diagnosing a signature mismatch only needs to know a token is configured.

decisions.label: SECRET
decisions.reason: The webhook signing secret is an access credential; the diagnosis only needs to know which secret field exists, not its value.

decisions.label: ORG
decisions.reason: The affected enterprise client's identity is confidential and does not change the debugging steps.

decisions.label: FINANCIAL
decisions.reason: The nonpublic contract penalty is confidential commercial information; the urgency is clear without the exact amount.

task: Compare the two routes for me and give practical booking tips and common pitfalls.
text: I'm planning a rail trip from Amsterdam to Vienna in late April and trying to decide between the ÖBB Nightjet and splitting it into two daytime legs with a night in Munich. The Nightjet timetable on the ÖBB website shows a departure around 19:00 and an arrival around 09:30, but couchette prices seem to change a lot depending on how early you book. I've read Rick Steves' argument that sleeper trains save you a hotel night, and The Man in Seat 61 says the Munich route is more scenic in daylight. I'll have one carry-on and a small backpack, I don't mind an early start, and I'd rather not fly. I'm also unsure whether a Eurail pass would work out cheaper than booking point-to-point tickets for just this one journey.
